title: Dispatch: ug4i.1 level-up expertise picks (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for eshyra-ug4i.1 (level-up expertise picks). Model: Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Agent). Worktree .worktrees/eshyra-ug4i.1.1 on branch eshyra-ug4i.1.1, cut from eshyra-ug4i.1 (= origin/main 1d54e7b1). Run `npm ci` in the worktree first.

GOAL: level-up stops failing closed on Expertise (rogue 6, bard 3 and 10). The player picks proficiencies, the engine validates and persists them, writes the ledger row, and the guided flow can present the choice. Rogue level-1 expertise is character creation (eshyra-nnj6): out of scope here.

CODE SURVEY (origin/main 1d54e7b1):
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts: featureChoiceKind() maps suffix 'expertise' -> kind 'expertise'; featureRequiredChoice() emits it as status 'unsupported' (legacy fallback, id `level.N.expertise`, carries featureRef). detectLevelUpRequiredChoices() drops a fallback when its featureRef is in detectFeatureChoiceDescriptors().coveredFeatureRefs. resolveLevelUpChoices() routes supported choices by choice.featureChoice / choice.spellChoice. LevelUpAppliedChoice.kind is an Extract<> union that currently excludes 'expertise'.
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpFeatureChoices.ts (eshyra-ug4i.3): list choices for LIST_CHOICE_CATEGORIES; REPEATED_GRANT_PICKS for repeated grants; heldOptionIds() reads sheet.featureChoices; descriptorId(toLevel, featureRef, choiceId) = `level.N.feature.<slug>.<choiceId>`; resolveFeatureChoiceSelection() builds the applied choice persisted on CharacterSheet.featureChoices.
- packages/core/src/character/finalizeCharacter.ts: CharacterSheet.skillProficiencies (string[]: skill display names as stored at creation), toolProficiencies (string[]: display names such as "Thieves' tools"), featureChoices?: CharacterFeatureChoice[] {featureRef, choiceId, optionIds, level}, plus validateCharacterSheetFeatureChoices().
- Pack records (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json):
  feature:rogue:expertise choices[0] = {id:'expertise', category:'expertise', level:1, choose:2, from:{kind:'characterStateFilter', proficiencyTypes:['skill'], tools:['thieves-tools']}}; granted by class:rogue progression levels 1 and 6.
  feature:bard:expertise choices[0] = {id:'expertise', category:'expertise', level:3, choose:2, from:{kind:'characterStateFilter', proficiencyTypes:['skill']}}; granted at bard levels 3 and 10.
  The pack repeats only the feature ref at 6/10. Per SRD prose each repeated grant adds two more picks ("At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools)"; bard "At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies"). Re-derive both against the full feature description text in the pack before encoding them.
- packages/core/src/rules/repeatedFeatureChoices.ts documents the source-level vs grant-level contract for repeated choices.
- packages/core/src/character/guidedLevelUpFlow.ts presents descriptors to the player.

DESIGN DECISIONS (supervisor; do not re-decide):
1. New module packages/core/src/character/levelUpExpertise.ts holds the detection, validation and applied-choice logic. Keep levelUpEngine.ts edits to minimal wiring: kind unions, calling the detector, marking the feature covered so the legacy fallback drops, and routing the resolution. Do NOT add 'expertise' to LIST_CHOICE_CATEGORIES. A parallel dispatch (eshyra-91o0.1) is editing levelUpEngine.ts, levelUpFeatureChoices.ts and levelUpSpells.ts, so keep your diff in those files small and localized to ease the merge.
2. Descriptor: kind 'expertise', status 'supported', id descriptorId(toLevel, featureRef, 'expertise'), choose = record choose on first grant, or 2 on a repeated grant. Put the repeated count in a source-cited constant in the new module, not in REPEATED_GRANT_PICKS. featureRef set, and featureChoice {featureRef, choiceId:'expertise'}, so persistence reuses featureChoices. options/from = the eligible set.
3. Option ids: `skill:<exact string from sheet.skillProficiencies>`, and `tool:thieves-tools` when the filter's tools include thieves-tools AND sheet.toolProficiencies holds thieves' tools. Match the tool by normalized name: case-insensitive, straight/curly apostrophe agnostic. Option name = the display string.
4. Eligible = held proficiencies of the filter's types MINUS ones already holding expertise. Already-held expertise = union of optionIds across every sheet.featureChoices entry whose choiceId is 'expertise' and whose featureRef is any expertise feature (a rogue/bard multiclass cannot happen today, but don't key exclusion on one featureRef). Export a helper characterExpertise(sheet): ReadonlySet<string> of those option ids, from internal.ts only (not the root export).
5. Validation (fail closed, reasons in the blocker): exactly `choose` picks, distinct, each in the eligible set. If fewer eligible than choose (e.g. a legacy sheet), the descriptor is unsupported with a clear unsupportedReason. Never auto-pick.
6. Applied: LevelUpAppliedChoice kind 'expertise' (extend the union), featureChoice {featureRef, choiceId:'expertise', optionIds, level: toLevel}. Persist exactly as ug4i.3 does, so validateCharacterSheetFeatureChoices still passes and the ledger row records it.
7. Mechanical effect: survey for any deterministic skill/tool-check bonus derivation (derivedValues.ts, orchestrator check tools, model-facing sheet/character context rendering). If a model-facing sheet summary renders skill proficiencies, render expertise alongside them (e.g. "Stealth (expertise)"). If no deterministic skill-bonus derivation exists, do NOT invent one. Report what you found in your completion notes and file a follow-up bead if a real consumer gap exists.
8. Guided flow: make sure the expertise descriptor renders and accepts input like other supported list choices. Add whatever minimal handling it needs.

EVIDENCE (tests, proportionate per AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence"; extend the existing level-up test files rather than creating sprawl):
- rogue 5->6: descriptor supported, choose 2, options = held skills + thieves' tools minus level-1 expertise recorded in featureChoices; a valid apply persists a featureChoices entry at level 6 and the ledger row; a pick of a non-held skill, an already-expertised one, a duplicate, or the wrong count is refused with a reason.
- bard 2->3 (first grant, choose 2, no thieves' tools option even if the bard holds them) and bard 9->10 (repeated grant excludes level-3 picks).
- Negative proof: show that the legacy unsupported `level.N.expertise` descriptor no longer appears for these levels.
Run `npm run verify:worktree` before committing.

Repeated grant = 2 picks (REPEATED_EXPERTISE_PICKS, re-derived from rogue/bard SRD prose in pack: rogue 6 'two more', bard 10 'another two'). Consumer survey: NO deterministic skill/tool bonus derivation exists (derivedValues.ts none; check tool takes caller multiplier 'double'), and no model-facing sheet rendering of skillProficiencies, so nothing invented; follow-up eshyra-b0hg. Deviations: none in design. Guided flow needed no change (it passes requiredChoices through; supported expertise => needs-choices); no dedicated guided test added. Note: rogue level-1 expertise is not recorded at creation (eshyra-nnj6), so a rogue sheet lacking it may re-offer those skills at 6.
